chapter_title: The Second, concerning the Parable of the Tree.

15.original: [They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.]
15.content: They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.

spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Two Trees (Kephalaia — Oldest Teaching Layer)

---

**¶11:** [GAP-1: *spiritual sense requires an opening invocation or framing address*] how I will open to your interior understanding [GAP-2: *the spiritual sense requires an object of revelation — likely the nature or mystery of the two perceptions*] the one who unfolds the interior meaning [GAP-3: *continuation of the agent who discloses*] — the systems of perception and understanding [GAP-4: *likely a description or enumeration of these perceptions*]. The Divine Love itself [GAP-5: *the spiritual sense requires a verbal action of the Divine toward these perceptions*] all of them, as He [GAP-6: *an action of ordering or establishing*] in the [GAP-7: *a qualifier — likely "whole" or "external"*] natural mind [GAP-8: *possibly a transition or elaboration*]. This perception rooted in divine wisdom, the [GAP-9: *an epithet or quality of this good perception*] — the wisdom radiating from this good perception [GAP-10: *likely a verb of ascent, connection, or manifestation*] the sustaining column of divine truth [GAP-11: *likely a further description of the column's function or destination*].

---

**¶12:** [GAP-12: *the spiritual sense requires a connective or further identification*] The rational truths that are clothed upon the external understanding [GAP-13: *likely "of" or "belonging to"*] of this perception rooted in divine wisdom. They are the particles of divine wisdom that are dispersed and intermixed throughout the whole of the mind.

---

**¶14:** Behold, this is the perception rooted in divine wisdom [GAP-14: *the spiritual sense requires a concluding epithet, summary, or transition to the next teaching*].

---

**¶15:** [GAP-15: *likely a transitional address or conjunction*] I open to your interior understanding [GAP-16: *the spiritual sense requires an identification of what is being revealed — the faculties of the good perception*] — it possesses five ascending faculties. [GAP-17: REVIEW — They are initial reflection, deliberation, perception of truth, interior understanding, and inmost will.] [GAP-18: REVIEW — Its deliberation] is the sustaining order of divine truth, the fully regenerated spiritual form. [Its perception of truth is the primordial divine wisdom] that abides within the doctrinal vessel of living truth. Its interior understanding is the mediating divine influx [GAP-19: REVIEW — that abides within] the doctrinal vessel of celestial love, which illuminates throughout [GAP-20: *the spiritual sense requires the sphere or domain illuminated — likely "all states" or "the whole mind"*]. And the inmost will is the Divine Love itself, that abides in infinite fullness, perfect throughout the heavenly realms of wisdom.

---

**¶17:** It is initial reflection that shall [GAP-21: *the spiritual sense requires a verb of gathering, lifting, or beginning the ascent — this is the first faculty that initiates the elevation*] — they shall be elevated [GAP-22: *the spiritual sense requires the destination: "to deliberation, which"*] is deliberation; they shall be elevated to perception of truth, which is the primordial divine wisdom that abides within the doctrinal vessel for obscure states; from perception of truth they shall ascend to interior understanding, which is the mediating divine influx that abides within the doctrinal vessel for illuminated states. And this also — the grand and radiant interior understanding — shall conduct them into the inmost will, which is the Divine Love itself, the God of all truth, the infinite Will governing all the heavenly realms of divine splendor.

---

**¶19:** [GAP-23: *the spiritual sense requires a transition — likely "Now concerning the"*] evil [GAP-24: *perception or system — "tree" in natural sense*] that [GAP-25: *likely "exists" or "operates"*] within [GAP-26: *likely "the natural mind" or "the external states"*] — also [GAP-27: *a connective or qualifier*] — in the manner that [GAP-28: *the spiritual sense requires a verb of correspondence or parallel: "is opposite to" or "inverts"*] the perception rooted in divine wisdom [GAP-29: *a transitional phrase*] — of self-love [GAP-30: *likely a verb — "from which" or "out of which proceed"*] they are the dominant evil loves [GAP-31: *that govern or rule over*] the interior states and the recurring cycle of natural existence [GAP-32: *likely a connective*] — they are the five proprial desires of the selfhood that proceed through [GAP-33: *likely the world or natural states*] — producing works [GAP-34: *that constitute*] doctrine of falsity, the hidden principle of deception that [GAP-35: *the spiritual sense requires an agent clause*] the ruling evil established within the natural mind.

---

**¶22:** [GAP-36: *the spiritual sense requires: "Now I will"*] open to your interior understanding, and you [GAP-37: *likely "shall perceive" or "shall understand"*]. The perception rooted in evil possesses five descending faculties. They are initial compulsion, scheming, false perception, infernal reasoning, and inmost evil will. Its initial compulsion is the governing principle of spiritual death. Its scheming is the restless cycling through successive forms of falsity [GAP-38: *likely "passing"*] from one persuasion of evil to another. Also, its false perception is the consuming heat of self-love [GAP-39: *the spiritual sense requires "which is"*] the infernal state, which is dense with falsity from evil. Its infernal reasoning [GAP-40: *likely "is a" or "becomes the"*] containing form of evil. Its inmost evil will is the [GAP-41: *the spiritual sense requires an epithet — perhaps "the final state" or "the uttermost depth"*] — the consolidated mass of all evils, the final spiritual captivity, the [GAP-42: *another epithet for the ultimate infernal bond*] — those states that the ruling evil expelled [GAP-43: *likely "into" or "from"*] the great [GAP-44: *likely "abyss" or "depth of falsity"*] — and they descend [GAP-45: *likely "into"*] utter falsity and spiritual blindness [GAP-46: *likely "consuming" or "destroying"*] all [GAP-47: *likely "that remains of wisdom within them"*] — and they strip away [GAP-48: *likely "every remaining truth" or "all good"*] — are absorbed into the consolidated mass of evil, and they are held in spiritual captivity [GAP-49: *likely "by" or "within"*] — the works of utter falsity, which they [GAP-50: *likely "produce" or "perpetuate"*] to eternity without end [GAP-51: *likely a connective or elaboration*]. The essential interior quality [GAP-52: *of the one who descends — likely "of anyone who"*] will reach that infernal state, and there is no turning or conversion of will possible there.

---

**¶23:** [GAP-53: *likely "Now" or "So then"*] — this is the unfolding of the perception rooted in evil, as I have disclosed to you, which you [GAP-54: *likely "now understand" or "have received"*] concerning it [GAP-55: *a transition: likely "that a good perception cannot produce"*] — good works [GAP-56: *likely "nor can an evil perception bring forth anything but"*] — its works are evil [GAP-57: *likely "and all that is produced"*] within it, throughout all its states of duration [GAP-58: *likely "remains evil" or "bears only evil"*] within it.

---

**¶24:** — it being transformed from [GAP-59: *the spiritual sense requires "its root nature" or "its origin"*] — which is grounded in the mind disposed to receive good and truth [GAP-60: *the spiritual sense requires "where there is only spiritual"*] vitality and wisdom; since spiritual death and falsity have no being [GAP-61: *likely "within that ground" or "in that receptive mind"*]. Also, the perception rooted in evil is the merely natural unregenerate selfhood [GAP-62: *likely a connective: "and concerning"*] it — I perceive it as standing alone among the [GAP-63: *the spiritual sense requires "perceptions or states"*] which arises in the mind disposed to receive evil and falsity [GAP-64: *likely "where there is only"*] falsity and spiritual death.

---

**¶25:** [GAP-65: *the spiritual sense requires: "Whoever perceives the distinction between"*] these two systems of perception, and distinguishes them from one another — he perceives that good did not originate from evil, nor evil from good. They did not proceed from one another. They did not proceed from a single source! The one who can make this distinction may ascend to the heavenly realm of wisdom.

---

**¶26:** And he perceives [GAP-66: *likely "that from the good perception"*] — evil works did not originate from it [GAP-67: *likely "nor good works from the evil"*]; but whoever cannot distinguish [GAP-68: *likely "good from evil" or "these two perceptions"*] from one another, descends into the state of utter falsity and spiritual blindness [GAP-69: *likely "and remains there"*] until he arrives at the [GAP-70: *the spiritual sense requires the final infernal state — "the ultimate depth of captivity" or "the consolidated mass of evil from which there is no return"*].

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [Listen] how I will reveal to you [the two trees, I] the expound[er of] the trees [that] the Father [planted] all of them, as he [set them] in the [whole] world [now concerning] this good tree, the [life] the light of this good tree [rises to] the Pillar [of Glory]
[And these are] the intellectuals that are cloaked upon its body [of] this good tree. They are the light elements that are mingled, being compounded in the totality.
Behold, this is the good tree [as I have explained to you]

[Also] I reveal to you [that] it has five limbs. [They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.] [Its counsel] is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man. [Its insight is the Fir]st Man who dwells in the ship of living waters. Its thought is the Third Ambassador [who dwells in] the ship of living fire, that shines in [the heavens] Also, the mind is the Father who dwells in greatness, who is perfect in the aeons of light.

It is consideration that shall [gather them, and] they shall be raised up [to the Pillar, which] is counsel; they shall be raised up to insight, which is the First Man who dwells in the ship of the night; from insight they shall rise up to thought, which is the Ambassador who dwells in the ship of the day. And he too, great glorious thought, shall bring them in to mind; which is the Father, the God of truth, the great Mind of all the aeons of glory.

[Now concerning the] bad [tree. The things that] happen in [the world] from [the darkness] also [in] the way that it is [opposite to] the good tree [and the works] of the fire [from which] they are the ruling-power [over] heaven and the wheel [also] they are the five fleshes that walk [in the world, and their] fruit [is the te]aching as of error, the mystery that [he established, wh]ich Satan appointed in the world.

[Now I will] reveal to you and you [shall understand] The bad tree has five limbs. They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind. Its consideration is the law of death. Its counsel is transmigration [passing] in type after type. Also, its insight is the furnaces of fire [which is ge]henna; which is full of smoke. Thought [is the] vessel. Its mind is the [tomb] the lump, the last bond, the [prison], they that Satan cast away [into] the great [fire] and they fall [into] the darkness [destroying] all [that is good] and they take away [the light, and] are swallowed in to the lump, and they are bound [in] the fruit of darkness, the one that they [bear] for ever and ever [without seeing] his face [of anyone who] will arrive at that place; and they have no repentance therein.

[Now] this is the explanation of the bad tree, as I have explained to you, which you [have received] to it [a good tree cannot make] good fruit [bad, nor the bad tree] its fruit bad [good. All that is] in it, in its existent days [is evil] in it.

it being changed from [its root] which lies in its good earth [in which there is life] and light; as death and darkness do not exist [in it] Also, the bad tree is Matter [and concerning] it, I understand it alone among the [things wh]ich occurs in its bad earth [in which there is] darkness and death.

[Whoever knows] these two trees, and separates them one from another. He understands that they did not arise out of one another, nor did they come from one another. They did not come from one another. They did not come from one! The person who can separate them out may go up to the aeon of light,

And he sees [that from the good tree] bad fruit did not arise from it [nor good fruit from the bad]; but whoever will not separate out [these two trees] from one another, he falls to the land of darkness [and remains there] until he arrives at the [lump]

fills.explanation: The Kephalaia consistently opens new teachings with "Listen" as the teacher's address to disciples, and the spiritual sense requires an opening invocation.

The object of revelation is "the two trees" (matching the spiritual sense's "the two perceptions"), followed by "I" beginning Mani's self-identification as the expounder: "I will reveal to you the two trees — I, the expounder of the trees that the Father planted."
Completes "expounder of" — the agent who discloses the meaning of "the trees" which immediately follows.
Relative pronoun connecting "the trees" to the Father's action: "the trees that the Father planted, all of them" — standard Coptic relative clause construction with resumptive pronoun.
The most natural verb for the Father's creative action within the tree metaphor: "the trees that the Father planted, all of them" — the divine origin of the good tree's structures.
Complements "planted" with the placement action: "as he set them in the whole world" — the Father placed the light elements into the mixed cosmos, a central Manichaean cosmological event.
Standard qualifier: "in the whole world" — emphasizing the totality of the cosmos into which the Father's plantings are distributed.
Transitional phrase parallel to GAP-23's "Now concerning the" for the bad tree; shifts focus from the Father's planting in the world to the specific identification of the good tree.

The good tree is identified as "the life" — the first of the fundamental Manichaean pair, confirmed by ¶24's own vocabulary: "in which there is life and light." Life is the epithet; light is what rises to the Pillar.
The light of the good tree ascends through the Column of Glory — the central Manichaean cosmological process whereby purified light particles travel upward through the Pillar to the realm of light.
"The Pillar of Glory" is the standard Manichaean cosmological term, attested in ¶15 of this same chapter as "the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man."

Standard Kephalaia identification formula opening a new paragraph: "And these are the intellectuals that are cloaked upon its body" — introducing a class of beings, followed by the parallel "They are the light elements."
Genitive connector: "cloaked upon its body of this good tree" — standard Coptic appositional genitive identifying whose body is meant.

fills.fill: as I have explained to you
fills.explanation: Parallels the concluding formula for the bad tree in ¶23: "the explanation of the bad tree, as I have explained to you" — the same summarizing phrase closes the good tree's identification section.
Standard Kephalaia transitional conjunction introducing a new point within the same teaching; ¶14 identified the good tree and ¶15 now reveals its internal structure.
Simple conjunction linking "I reveal to you" to the content clause "it has five limbs," with the referent (the good tree) already established in ¶14.

fills.fill: They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.
fills.original: They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.
fills.explanation: REVIEW CONFIRMED: The editor's five terms match exactly the ascending sequence used throughout ¶17 and ¶22, and correspond to the five discrete degrees of the mind from outermost reflection to inmost will.

REVIEW CONFIRMED: Consideration (the lowest faculty) serves as the starting point of ascent without a cosmic mapping; the identifications begin with counsel, the second faculty, mapped to the Pillar of Glory.
REVIEW CONFIRMED: The formulaic pattern "X who dwells in Y" is used identically for the First Man (ship of living waters), the Third Ambassador (ship of living fire), and the Father (greatness).
The Third Ambassador shines from the ship of living fire (the sun) across the celestial realm; "the heavens" is the domain illuminated by this cosmic figure in Manichaean cosmology.

Consideration is the first faculty that initiates the ascent by collecting the scattered light elements; "gather" is the standard Manichaean term for the initial soteriological action before elevation.

The ascending pattern requires the first destination after consideration; the Pillar of Glory (identified as counsel in ¶15) is the cosmic structure through which light ascends, yielding "raised up to the Pillar, which is counsel."
Standard Kephalaia transitional formula introducing a new subject; the teaching shifts from the good tree to the bad tree.
Names the bad tree (as required by the spiritual sense) and bridges to "happen" with a standard Kephalaia construction: "the bad tree. The things that happen in the world."
The bad tree's effects manifest "in the world" — the mixed cosmos where light and darkness are intermingled, the standard Manichaean domain for the operation of evil.
The bad tree's manifestations in the world originate "from the darkness" — the fundamental Manichaean source of evil, contrasting with the good tree's origin in life and light.
Grammatically required preposition: "also in the way that it is opposite to the good tree" — the only construction that yields a coherent modal clause.
The bad tree's structure is the inversion of the good tree: "the way that it is opposite to the good tree" — fundamental Manichaean dualism where darkness mirrors and opposes light in every respect.

Transitional phrase bridging from the good tree contrast to the fire-element: "opposite to the good tree, and the works of the fire" — introducing the archonic manifestations of the bad tree's destructive element.
Relative connector: "the works of the fire, from which they are the ruling-power" — the archonic ruling-powers derive their nature from the destructive works of the fire-element.
The archonic forces exercise dominion: "the ruling-power over heaven and the wheel" — the demonic powers rule over the celestial sphere and the zodiacal cycle in Manichaean cosmology.

Standard Kephalaia transition between parallel identifications: "the ruling-power over heaven and the wheel. Also, they are the five fleshes" — moving from celestial to terrestrial manifestations of the same evil forces.
The five fleshes walk "in the world" (their domain of operation in Manichaean cosmology), and "their" connects to "fruit" which follows, introducing the evil works they produce.
Completes "their fruit is the teaching as of error" — identifying the fruit of the five fleshes as false doctrine, with "te" + "aching" forming "teaching."

Standard Coptic construction where a pronoun is later clarified by the full noun in a relative clause: "the mystery that he established, which Satan appointed in the world" — with "wh" + "ich" forming "which."
Standard Kephalaia revelatory formula introducing a new teaching section; parallels the chapter's recurring pattern of "I will reveal to you."
Standard Manichaean teacher-student formula: "I will reveal to you and you shall understand" — the promise of comprehension following revelation.
The participial "passing" connects "transmigration" to "in type after type," describing the soul's restless cycling through successive bodily forms — the standard Manichaean metempsychosis teaching.
Appositional identification: "the furnaces of fire, which is gehenna" — "ge" joins with "henna" to form "gehenna," the standard term for the infernal fires in Manichaean eschatology.
Follows the parallel identification pattern used throughout: "Its counsel is transmigration," "its insight is the furnaces of fire" — so "Thought is the vessel."
Standard Kephalaia eschatological triad: tomb, lump, last bond — the tomb is the place of permanent death and confinement, appearing regularly in Manichaean lists of the final infernal state.

Completes the eschatological series: tomb, lump, last bond, prison — "the prison" denotes the ultimate confinement, semantically extending "the last bond" and collocating naturally with "they that Satan cast away into" the great fire.
Directional preposition: "they that Satan cast away into the great [fire/abyss]" — the standard Manichaean formula for the expulsion of evil into its final confinement.
"The great fire" is a standard Manichaean eschatological term for the final conflagration, the culmination beyond the "furnaces of fire" and "gehenna" already mentioned for the insight-limb.
Directional preposition completing "they fall into the darkness" — the standard Manichaean formula for descent into the realm of evil.
Participial action of the evil forces in their descent: "they fall into the darkness, destroying all that is good" — simultaneous with the fall, they annihilate whatever good remains.

Specifies what the darkness destroys: "all that is good" — corresponding to the spiritual reading's "all that remains of wisdom within them," rendered in the Kephalaia's natural vocabulary of good versus evil.
Standard Manichaean concept: the evil forces strip away the remaining light before being themselves sealed into the lump — "they take away the light, and are swallowed in to the lump."
Locative preposition: "they are bound in the fruit of darkness" — describing spiritual captivity within the consolidated evil, parallel to being "swallowed in to the lump."

Tree-metaphor verb: "the fruit of darkness, the one that they bear for ever and ever" — the evil beings perpetually produce evil fruit, consistent with the chapter's teaching that each tree bears only its own kind.
Describes the eternal state of the damned: "they bear the fruit of darkness for ever and ever, without seeing his face" — perpetual separation from God, never beholding the divine countenance.

Matches the spiritual reading exactly: "the face of anyone who will arrive at that place" — in Coptic idiom, "the face of anyone who" means "the person/destiny of anyone who" reaches the infernal state.
Transitional marker introducing the summary: "Now, this is the explanation of the bad tree" — standard Kephalaia recapitulation formula.
Completes the teacher-student formula: "which you have received" — the disciples have received the explanation, and "to it" (concerning it) then introduces the dual principle about fruit.
First half of the Matthew 7:17-18 principle: a good tree cannot make its good fruit become bad — each tree's nature is fixed and cannot be corrupted or improved.
Second half of the dual principle, with verb elision typical of Coptic parallel clauses: "nor [can] the bad tree [make] its bad fruit [good]" — completing the symmetrical impossibility.
"Good" completes the dual principle (bad fruit cannot become good), then "All that is" introduces the concluding summary about the tree's fixed nature throughout its existence.

Concludes the bad tree's characterization: "All that is in it, in its existent days, is evil in it" — everything within the bad tree throughout its duration remains evil without possibility of change.
The good tree is "changed from its root which lies in its good earth" — the root is the origin grounded in the receptive mind of good and truth, paralleling the tree/earth imagery throughout.

Completes the description of the good earth: "its good earth, in which there is life and light" — the two positive qualities (life and light) contrasted with death and darkness in the following clause.
Locative closure: "death and darkness do not exist in it" — confirming the exclusive presence of life and light in the good earth.
Connective introducing the parallel analysis of the bad tree: "the bad tree is Matter, and concerning it, I understand it alone" — shifting from identification to examination.
Completes "among the things which occurs in its bad earth" — "wh" + "ich" forms "which"; the bad tree is understood uniquely among the things arising from the ground of evil.
Parallel to GAP-60 for the good earth: "its bad earth, in which there is darkness and death" — the two negative qualities contrasting with life and light.

Conditional opening introducing the soteriological test: "Whoever knows these two trees, and separates them" — knowledge of the distinction between good and evil is the prerequisite for spiritual ascent.
The one who separates the trees perceives "that from the good tree, bad fruit did not arise from it" — confirming the impossibility of evil originating from good.

fills.fill: nor good fruit from the bad
fills.explanation: Completes the dual impossibility: bad fruit cannot come from the good tree, nor good fruit from the bad — the principle that the two origins are absolutely separate.

The warning counterpart: "whoever will not separate out these two trees from one another" — failing to distinguish the two systems leads to descent, paralleling "whoever knows these two trees" in GAP-65.
Describes the consequence of failing to separate: falling to the land of darkness and remaining there — the state of spiritual captivity preceding the final infernal destination.
The "lump" (bolos) is the Manichaean term for the consolidated mass of all evil at the end of time — the ultimate infernal destination described earlier in ¶22 as "the lump, the last bond."
